authority: evidence-only; a component names what to look for. It is not a finding, a grade, a chart position or an adoption decision.
purpose: The named components of collaborative intelligence that StaleToast searches and compares sources against. Claims (CI-###) remain the unit of evidence and the named gap of a round; a component says which part of a collaborative system a source is about.

owner_instruction.summary: Expand the search scope with the missing aspects as additional categories and components of collaborative intelligence.

statuses.established: Compared against retained sources in the baseline artifact. Its screen terms and comparison question are copied from that artifact and must not drift from it.
statuses.added-unscreened: Added to scope. Its search terms and queries are proposals that have not been run. It holds no screened source, routing count or finding.

rules: A daily or monthly round records one component id alongside its named gap. The claim-based gap order in the appraisal priorities is unchanged.
For an added-unscreened component, screen the existing retained pool against its screen terms before any new discovery. New discovery follows only where that screen leaves the component thin.
Queries listed under an added-unscreened component are proposals. Record the queries actually run, their dates and their counts in the dated batch artifact, as for any other round.
A component moves to established only when a dated routing artifact compares retained sources against it. Update baseline_artifact in the same change.
Adding a component changes no catalog record, appraisal, chart position, export or daily limit.
Keep every component public and generic. A component describes a mechanism, never a private system.
related_claims_meaning: A pointer to claims a component is likely to inform. It is not an evidence link and adds no support to any claim.

components.label: Authority and handoff
components.definition: Who may act, on what, under whose approval, and how that passes intact from one person or agent to the next.
components.comparison_question: Does the source add a check at a boundary our control record only describes?

components.label: Memory and correction
components.definition: What a system keeps between sessions, how it retrieves it, and how a corrected or superseded fact stops being used.
components.comparison_question: Does the source improve retrieval or update behavior without losing source versions, correction survival or access boundaries?

components.label: Recovery and replay
components.definition: How interrupted, failed or duplicated work is detected, attributed and resumed without repeating its effects.
components.comparison_question: Does this provide a better failure drill or attribution method than our current evidence replay?

components.label: Evaluation and evidence
components.definition: How a result is checked against a baseline, and what evidence supports calling it done.
components.comparison_question: Does it supply executable checks or better measurement that the existing method leaves to an adopter?

components.label: Provenance and data diff
components.definition: Where a result came from, which source version it used, and exactly what changed between two versions.
components.comparison_question: Does it expose a source-to-result or row-level change that hashes and counts alone miss?

components.label: Cost and coordination burden
components.definition: Tokens, time, rework and human attention spent, including the overhead that coordination itself adds.
components.comparison_question: Can it reduce observed work or inspection cost without trading away correctness or authority?

components.label: Cross-harness tracing
components.definition: Following one piece of work across different tools and agents with a record each of them can read.
components.comparison_question: Does it normalize useful evidence across tools without overcollecting private content or equating traces with authenticated completion?

components.label: Security and containment
components.definition: Limits on what an agent can read, run and change, and tests that those limits hold when the agent meets hostile or misleading content.
components.comparison_question: Does the source give a repeatable test that a stated limit holds under hostile or misleading input, rather than a description of the limit?

repository_queries.query: agent sandbox in:name,description fork:false archived:false stars:>=5

components.prior_coverage: The 2026-11-01 expansion searched the research topic agent-safety and the repository category agent-security. No component compared those sources to a containment baseline.
components.boundary: Defensive containment and its tests only. A source that emphasizes offensive technique, evasion, bypass or unverified access claims stays held for the separate scope and misuse-boundary appraisal recorded in the 2026-11-01 expansion. This component does not release a held source.

components.label: Deliberation and dissent
components.definition: Structured disagreement between agents, or between people and agents: independent first answers, bounded rounds, how a minority view is kept, and whether a second view changed the result.
components.comparison_question: Does the source measure whether a second independent view changed the outcome, against a single-agent baseline at comparable cost?

repository_queries.query: agent debate in:name,description fork:false archived:false stars:>=5

components.prior_coverage: The 2026-11-01 expansion searched the research topic multi-agent-systems. The terms multi-agent and coordination were screened under cross-harness-tracing, which asks about shared records, not about whether disagreement improved a result.
components.boundary: Agreement between agents is not verification. A source that reports only that agents converged does not answer the comparison question.

components.label: Learning from operation
components.definition: How a system changes its own rules, checks or prompts from its recorded failures and corrections, and how it shows that the change reduced repeats.
components.comparison_question: Does the source show a recorded failure becoming an enforced check with a measured drop in repeats, rather than a longer instruction file?

repository_queries.query: self-improving agent in:name,description fork:false archived:false stars:>=5
agent postmortem in:name,description fork:false archived:false stars:>=5

components.prior_coverage: No research topic or repository category searched for it. memory-and-correction covers a corrected fact, not a changed rule or check.
components.boundary: A system revising its own instructions is not independent verification that the revision helped. Model fine-tuning and weight updates are out of scope; this component covers changes to rules, checks, prompts and procedures.

components.label: Orchestration and automation
components.definition: Deciding which agent, model or tool does which part of a task and in what order, and running that on a schedule or trigger without a person starting each step.
components.comparison_question: Does the source show that its routing or scheduling rule beats a fixed single-agent assignment on the same task, with the rule open to inspection and its cost reported?
components.prior_coverage: The 2026-11-01 expansion searched the repository category workflow-runtime. No component asked whether a routing or scheduling rule beat a fixed assignment.
components.boundary: More agents are not a general advantage (CI-016). A source that adds a coordinating model without a single-agent comparison does not answer the comparison question.
